title: Factoring Polynomials of Degree 3 and 4
standard_text: 2A.7D determine the linear factors of a polynomial function of degree three and of degree four using algebraic methods; 2A.7E determine linear and quadratic factors of a polynomial expression of degree three and of degree four, including factoring the sum and difference of two cubes and factoring by grouping
meta_desc: Free Algebra II factoring worksheets for Texas TEKS 2A.7D and 2A.7E: sum and difference of cubes, grouping, quadratic form, the Factor Theorem and factoring completely. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: (x − c) is a factor when P(c) = 0.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Sum of cubes: a3 + b3 = (a + b)(a2 − ab + b2). Difference: a3 − b3 = (a − b)(a2 + ab + b2).
  • Grouping: factor pairs of terms, then factor out the common binomial.
  • Quadratic form: x4 − 5x2 + 4 is like u2 − 5u + 4 with u = x2.
  • Factor Theorem: (x − c) is a factor exactly when P(c) = 0. Divide by it to get the other factors.

Examples

Example

x3 + 3x2 − 4x − 12

x2(x + 3) − 4(x + 3)

(x + 3)(x2 − 4)

Answer: (x + 3)(x − 2)(x + 2)

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Wrong signs in a cubes patternDifference: (a − b)(a2 + ab + b2).
Not factoring completelyx2 − 4 still factors.
Testing the wrong numberFor (x + 3), find P(−3).
